accepted.title: Leading constant for the multistage triangle game with stop
accepted.text: Start with the board E(K_n) and winning sets the three-edge sets of triangles. In each stage Maker moves first, claiming one free edge per turn, and Breaker then claims at most one free edge. Stop the stage immediately when Maker has claimed a whole triangle, before the next Breaker turn. Remove only the edges claimed by Breaker in that stage; retain all Maker edges and all still free edges as the next board, and reset the ownership of retained edges for the next stage. Continue with triangles fully contained in the current board. If Maker cannot complete a triangle in a stage, the game terminates. Let τ_stop(n) be the maximum number of successful stages Maker can guarantee against every Breaker strategy. Determine whether τ_stop(n)/n² has a limit and, if it does, its value.
accepted.subject: Combinatorics & Graph Theory
accepted.citation: Problem 7.3.2, explicit H=K₃, b=1 clause; printed p. 137 / held PDF p. 145.
accepted.scope_review: Actual held physical pages 27–31 and 144–145 and current paper Section 8 define the game. Only the explicitly singled-out triangle/unbiased clause is promoted. The broader arbitrary-H wording has a trivial one-edge obstruction: Maker wins immediately without a Breaker move, so the board never shrinks. No extra hypothesis is silently inserted. Resetting ownership follows the instruction that each stage is a new Maker–Breaker game. Counting successful stages rather than the final failed stage changes duration by at most one and leaves the requested n² constant unchanged.
accepted.literature_finding: The 2023 revised primary retains Problem 8.4 and explicitly singles out H=K₃, b=1. Its Θ(n²) observation gives the scale, not the leading constant. No exact constant or refutation was located in the dated bounded primary scan.
accepted.duplicate_review: Whole live catalog family search found no multistage positional-game target. Q1256 is a static transversal two-factor existence problem. Independent full word/character retrieval and scope review required before numbering.
accepted.unpromoted_remainder: Other fixed graphs H and constant biases b in Problem 7.3.2 remain unreviewed. The one-edge case is degenerate and does not support a finite n² formula; no repaired general hypothesis is presumed.
